Commentary.Commentary: They faced similar pitches in the West Indies where they won the final, but most of those wins on slow tracks came when they were batting first. They have got a tough ask in front.
It is definitely not an easy pitch to bat on. Australia will need to get off to a good start with the new balls but then will have to resort to grafting and pushing once the balls get older.

Chandimal played brilliantly, making an unbeaten 80 on this difficult track. He took Sri Lanka past the 225-run mark with the average score on this ground being 234 in day/night ODIs. Faulkner finished with a 4-fer while Starc bagged 3. Zampa will be disappointed with his efforts, failing to get even a single wicket on a track which is helping the spinners.

That is a handy score from Sri Lanka on a difficult track. They did not get off to the best of starts, losing Kusal Perera and Dilshan early but then Mendis and Chandimal fought hard with a 79-run stand. However, Faulkner's double-wicket maiden got Australia back into the game.
Full and wide outside off, driven through point for a run. SRI LANKA FINISH ON 227/8!

OUT! Straight to the man! Full and outside off, Perera gets down and sweeps it straight to Josh Hazlewood at short fine leg.

FOUR! A length ball outside off, Dilruwan slashes hard and gets a thick inside edge past the stumps to fine leg!

OUT! 100 ODI WICKETS FOR STARC! And he is the fastest man on planet Earth to achieve this feat. The cutter from Starc, fuller and outside off, de Silva is way too early into his flick and the ball goes off the toe end of the bat. It spoons towards square leg where George Bailey runs across to his right from short mid-wicket and dives too take a good catch. Starc reaches the 100-wicket milestone in 52 ODIs, one less than Pakistan's Saqlain Mushtaq. Sri Lanka have now lost 3/8 in the last 20 balls.

There comes another cutter, a puff of dust arises from the spot where the ball lands, Mathews pushes at it but misses. Faulkner has a word or two with Mathews, who smiles. Then Faulkner smiles as well and now Chandimal sticks out his tongue and smiles too. Must have been a joke then.
On a good length around off, Mathews pushes at it but misses. Another slower ball from Faulkner.

OUT! Caught! Mendis departs and Australia finally have a wicket. The off cutter from Faulkner, just running his fingers over the side of the ball, landing it on a length outside off and getting it to angle away, Mendis looks to pull but plays it a tad early. Gets a top edge which is calmly taken by Travis Head jogging to his right at the edge of the circle around mid-wicket. Ends a promising innings from the youngster and the dangerous 79-run stand is broken.
JAMES FAULKNER is back on.

ANOTHER RUN OUT MISSED! Well... this is un-Australian like on the field. Aiming at the stumps but not hitting them. Smith comes charging in and has an under-arm flick but misses the stumps. Mendis was a goner again.

MENDIS WAS GONE WITH A DIRECT HIT. Another opportunity missed. The Australians have not been at their best on the field today. Chandimal pushes this towards point and sets off. Steven Smith comes charging in, looks have an under-arm flick at the striker's end but misses it by a long margin.

FOUR! Clever batting! Tossed up outside off, Mendis reaches out and sweeps it over square leg for a boundary! Knew where the fielders were.

TOP EDGE! SAFE AGAIN! Mendis is playing with his luck here. The captain is desperately trying to get the attention of his fielder. "FINCHY!" shouts Smith. No response. "FINCHYY!" yells the skipper. No response again. "FINCHYYYY!" is a bigger grunt. Now Finch sees and moves to the position suggested by his captain.

NOT OUT! Australia have used up their one review! Flighted on off, Mendis goes for a front foot defence but the ball spins in hits him on the pads. Zampa appeals with conviction but the umpire shakes his head. Steven Smith concurs and tries to dissuade Zampa but the bowler is adamant and Australia go for the review. The replays show that it was a legal delivery and everything looks fine until the ball tracking which shows that the ball was just about hitting the leg stump. It is umpire's call and the batsman gets another lease on life.
Review time! Zampa feels that Mendis is out LBW but the umpire doesn't think so. The bowler has forced Smith to take the review.

DROPPED! Outside off again, Chandimal looks to play it but gets an outside edge. It goes to the slips and Steven Smith leaps to his right to catch it. He doesn't have much time to react to it and the ball grazes his outstretched fingers and goes to third man for a brace.

OUT! IT'S UP IN THE AIR AND OUT! Fuller ball outside off, Dilshan goes for his trademark dilscoop. This time it goes wrong and it appears that the ball goes off his helmet and high behind the stumps. It comes down around first slip and Steven Smith comes running in and catches it. The umpire raises his finger and Dilshan walks off. However, the replays reveal something surprising. Dilshan goes down and attempts the scoop but misses. The ball to bounce up and hit him straight on the helmet. There was never any contact with the bat or gloves! It's a wonder that Dilshan never went for a review!
Full delivery on leg, driven through mid on.

NOT OUT! Flatter and outside off, Dilshan looks to play it and misses. The ball goes to the keeper who promptly removes the bails. The square leg umpire refers it upstairs and the replays show that Dilshan was comfortably in.
Floated on the stumps, Mendis flicks it through the leg side for a single.

Short and wide outside off, slapped to deep point for a single.

A short ball to start off, Mendis sways out of the way.
MOISES HENRIQUES is on as well as a double change.
Shortish delivery around off, worked to the leg side for a single.

Fuller ball around off, pushed to point.

Length ball on leg, Mendis flicks it through the leg side for a single.
In the corridor outside off, left alone.
FOUR! HOOKED! Another short delivery and Dilshan fully commits to it this time, pulling it through mid-wicket and sending it flying to the boundary. He is settling in well here.
Tillakaratne Dilshan now reaches the landmark of 1000 ODI runs against Australia!

Short outside off, Mendis cuts it through the covers.

Length ball outside off and angling in, defended off the back foot.
Full and outside off, Mendis pushes it to the covers.
Full delivery on off, driven through mid on.
Fuller ball around off, Dilshan looks to drive it to mid on but gets a bottom edge.

Fuller ball outside off, driven through the covers.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD to bowl with the second new ball..
Length ball outside off, Mendis opens the face of his bat and guides it to third man and gets off the mark with a single.
Full outside off, Starc makes the most of the swing. Mendis looks to play it but misses.
One of Sri Lanka's newest heroes, KUSAL MENDIS, walks in at number 3, replacing Kusal Perera.

OUT! STARC STRIKES! It's a jaffa out off, Perera crouches in his crease and looks to drive it down the ground but the ball shapes in just enough to beat his inside edge. It goes on to crash into the woodwork and uproots his off stump. Australia are off to an excellent start!
Down the leg side, Kusal looks to flick it but misses. The umpire signals a wide.
Fullish it length, Dilshan comes forward and looks to drive it and miscues it to backward point.
Fuller on middle and off, flicked to mid on.
Length ball on off, Perera looks to start things off with a front foot defence but gets an outside edge to square leg for a single.
The players are out in the middle. KUSAL PERERA and TILLAKARATNE DILSHAN are the openers for Sri Lanka and MITCHELL STARC will open the bowling proceedings.
Now, the Sri Lanka Matha is being sung at the stadium...
It is time for the national anthems. The visiting side's comes first, so up goes Advance Australia Fair...
Mathews says that he was looking to bat first anyways as the pitch would get worse as the day goes on. Informs that Sandakan and Aponso are making their ODI debuts.

Steven Smith says that it gets quite dewy in the evening, which is the prime reason for him opting to chase. Is assuming that the pitch will take turn from ball 1, as it is looking very dry. Does not quite name the starting XI and smartly avoids naming any.

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold says that the pitch looks very dry without any grass or even cracks. It could spin later in the evening. The new balls would be the easiest to play, says Arnold as the track would slow down which would make stroke-making tough.

TOSS - The news from out in the middle is that Steven Smith has won the toss and ahem... AUSTRALIA WILL BOWL FIRST. Interesting call, asking his players to brave the afternoon sun. There are some showers expected later in the day, so perhaps Smith expects D/L to come into play. Chasing becomes a better option then. As of now, not a cloud in the sky.

The Tests are done and dusted and it is now time for the limited over games. After the debacle with the red ball, Australia prepare themselves to face a barrage of spin with the white ball now as 5 ODIs and 2 T20Is come across to test them. They were ranked number 1 in the Tests before this tour, only to lose that courtesy a 3-0 whitewash. They are ranked number 1 in the ODIs as well... will the Lankans be able to afflict a similar result? As of now, a series win will be foremost on their minds. Hello and a warm welcome to the first ODI between Sri Lanka and Australia at Colombo.
